months.label: May 2026
entries: First solo security fix: endpoint with side effects was sitting on GET — turned down the temptation to make an exception, chose honest POST. If an action mutates state, the method must reflect it. Code and review in one day
Critical SMTP bug: service switching wasn't applying to all linked objects. Caught the root cause, wrote a helper synchronizer — the full path code→review→prod fit into one working day
Closed three long-running sagas at once: a task from December, one from March, and a redirect dragging on since 2024. Satisfying to clear debt that outlived whoever started it
distinct() was silently swallowing duplicates — non-deterministic results at production scale. 3 rounds of review: each round the solution simplified from overengineered to correct

Finalized the year-long external editor integration series: killed the visual jump on load by setting container dimensions before initialization. Bonus — a unified loader on DOM visibility monitoring, no timeouts or polling intervals
Webhook integration refactor: moved away from brittle substring matching to proper URL parsing, extracted configuration into constants, covered with unit tests. Prod and tests — same day

Handled EmptyResultSet explicitly instead of burying it under a bare except. Cyrillic in one of the forms was throwing 500 — added a pre-check before hitting the external service. Defensive programming as a habit

Lesson of the month: 16 hours of refactoring went to waste — the task became obsolete while I was doing it. Including a failed attempt via Claude Code. Note written: confirm the component's fate before starting major rework, not after

months.label: April 2026
entries: Proxy for a third-party visual editor: runtime interception of XHR and fetch inside an iframe with no access to its source — domain substitution on the fly, without touching a single line of third-party code. Most non-trivial solution to date; reviewer approved the architecture

SPF domain score API from scratch to prod in 3.5 days: recursive SPF record parsing, score calculation by rules, rating from D to A. Manually ran 30+ domains with a results table; magic numbers became named constants after review
SPF chain visualization page: AJAX without page reload, include-dependency tree with step-by-step breakdown, final score and matched rules — so DNS inheritance can be read at a glance, not guessed

Caught an XSS myself — not as part of the task, but as a side effect of deep analysis of another one. Sanitize-bypass via non-standard field type: documented, assessed risk, checked similar locations. Proactive security diagnosis instead of 'not my task'

months.label: March 2026
entries: Geo-filtering in segments: new operators 'contains / does not contain / empty / not empty'. Hit a CSS class conflict, caught and resolved it. Dependent MRs deployed in sync — getting the deploy order right

Root cause of 500-error in the send mechanism: wrong lookup field in an ORM query — syntactically valid on its own, but semantically wrong. Didn't just fix this one point, ran an audit across the whole codebase looking for the same class of error everywhere it could be hiding

Universal copy component instead of scattered ClipboardJS calls: added support for hidden values (passwords, tokens — copied but not exposed in the DOM). Walked all existing usages through the codebase and gradually migrated them to the unified mechanism

RFC email validation with inline errors: implementation with unit and integration tests. Along the way — an incident: code silently disappeared from stage due to an accidental revert. Rewrote the MR from scratch without panic, methodically, guided by the tests — context intact

Async Celery+Django task where it was easy to miss: log is written on save, then updated by the same ID after background recalculation. Tested under prod-like conditions — queues and periodic tasks simply don't run on stage

First time as a regular reviewer — five tasks in one month. Not rubber-stamp approvals: for one I dug into jQuery selector mechanics combined with django-widget-tweaks and wrote a substantive code breakdown

months.label: February 2026
entries: First reusable UI component: extracted modal dialogs into a shared module based on bootbox.js, applied to two different sections at once. On deploy, a Sentry alert fired — turned out to be a harmless stale cache, investigated and closed it myself. Bonus — first systematic documentation for the component

Counter for address corrections: two different edit paths, and bulk_create doesn't retain originals. Instead of carrying extra state, chose to count corrections without storing them — architectural decision approved in review

Popups inside a nested iframe of a third-party editor: modal and preview were fighting over z-index, height and overflow in someone else's context. Resolved with CSS isolation and careful context passing — non-trivial wrestling with iframe boundaries
Migrated static assets from external CDNs to self-hosted nginx. During testing, caught and fixed an unrelated bug — a minified component version had gone missing
Diagnosed two prod-only bugs that wouldn't reproduce locally. Carried both through to resolution in March — a lesson that prod-only bugs play by their own rules
Migration conflict when moving code: the original fix didn't get picked up. Resolved it myself, with a file backup before editing — careful iteration as a habit

months.label: January 2026
entries: Regex validation in a dynamic form: generating JS keys for fields, AJAX checking and server-side error return with precise highlighting of exactly the fields where errors occurred. Three iterations — rejected my own first solutions until I found something precise enough

Email validation per RFC: regex with careful strictness calibration. The first version was too strict and risked blocking valid addresses — rewrote it. Covered with unit tests and added an integration test for the API on my own initiative

Cyrillics decoding in JSON variables under Python 2.7: instead of workarounds — a wrapper class with overridden __str__/__repr__, resolving the str(dict) vs repr(dict) difference without breaking the interface. Along the way, extended special character protection across the whole project and discovered XSS through a legacy mark_safe on user-controlled input — documented and removed the risky path from the flow

months.label: December 2025
entries: Three critical bugs — three fixes on the day of discovery. A dashboard CSS failure went code→review→prod→test in 4 hours, using a minimally invasive inline fix to avoid disturbing parallel changes

Closed the longest investigation in my chronicle — failures in the background processing queue had been piling up for months. The ending wasn't code but knowledge: a document with diagrams, logs and a specific hypothesis, handed to the team. Formalized the next step as a separate task — it closed in March

Double-defect diagnosis: the first hypothesis gave a correct fix, but stage didn't pass. Dug deeper — found a second cause: AJAX was firing with the wrong context. Data was being saved correctly, just to the wrong place. Lesson: one symptom can hide two independent causes

XSS vulnerability surfaced while working on another task: assessed as low-risk DOM XSS, documented. Separately — two-layer form protection: after a reviewer's note about JS bypass, added a server-side layer and attached a DevTools demonstration of the bypass. Trust the client, verify on the server

Systematic QA of 25+ templates over two days using a checklist. Non-standard methods: DevTools Network Offline to simulate server failure, JS injection via console to emulate postback, manually setting status in the DB for a rare scenario. Along the way, found and removed a dead handler

Worked through the holidays Dec 24–29 — three tasks written in that period. Including a form edit where I got the wrong file: admitted it immediately, recreated the MR, prod same day. Wrote a Confluence article after the mistake — so the next person doesn't step on the same rake

months.label: November 2025
entries: End of a months-long editor series: instead of eight near-identical templates per tab — one universal one. Minus seven files and ~300 lines. Reviewer's note: 'The code came out clean.' Along the way — a stage incident from an unrelated migration, investigated independently and documented

EOL race: planned replacement of an expiring external dependency — done five weeks before the deadline. Three auth pages, a shared Django mixin for DRY, debugging a tricky naming issue (hyphen vs underscore). CI failure after first deploy — caught and fixed, honestly noting 'forgot about tests again'

Centralization of the dialog component: 29+ duplicates reduced to a single control point — changes across 37 files. Three-plus hours of self-testing across 30+ pages and a detailed testing guide for the QA team with each scenario described. A 'local' task that grew into a large one — a lesson in estimating scope

Detective story with a paginator: two defects plus a mysterious 302 redirect. Methodical hunt — curl, incognito, cookies, and finally Middleware as the culprit. Bonus — conflicts in minified JS resolved through a new branch: pragmatic, if not by the book. Case went into the notebook

months.label: October 2025
entries: Full integration cycle between two systems: designed it, got it to prod — and caught a production incident on prod itself (429 rate limit from an external API). Walked the path sync → async → cache on my own: identified the problem, understood its nature, chose the right fix

Security audit of the entire frontend layer: walked through 10+ apps looking for places where a user identifier could leak or be substituted. No existing algorithm — built the risk classification methodology myself, compiled results into a CSV report. A research task without a template, where half the work is figuring out what to look for

Search performance investigation: first time profiling via pyinstrument on a prod replica. Compared ILIKE vs REVERSE LIKE, reconsidered the approach after review — result: 8–10x speedup. Lesson of the month: the profiler shows truth you can't see with your eyes
Q4 series on the external editor: CSS feature flag, auto-preview, adaptive height

A pagination audit I consciously stopped: figured out and proved the task didn't need doing. Not a waste of time but an engineering decision — sometimes the most valuable result of an investigation is an argued 'leave it alone'

months.label: September 2025
entries: Compliance form with a hard deadline: 3 days planned — done in 2, prod without a single comment. First time feeling that a deadline isn't pressure, it's just a frame

Systemic investigation: thousands of undelivered emails had been accumulating since July. Pulled Celery worker logs and 5 years of git history, found the weak point — wrote a temporary fix that reduced the problem 6x, and extended logging to nail the root later
External service integration investigation: turned out the problem was on the partner's side, not ours — rate limiting. Instead of 'not our bug', found two workarounds
Comment mechanism refactor: three different implementations living in parallel — merged into one universal function. Not for cleanliness, but because a new feature couldn't be added otherwise
Old 500 bug (NoneType): uncovered that a 2023 commit silently broke an assumption made in 2020. Traced the full code history — review came back with 'ok, thanks for digging into this'

First solo stage deploy — and immediately an incident: migrations failed. Brought everything back up myself, didn't hide it, debugged the error openly and documented it. Lesson learned harder than a clean deploy would have taught it

18 hours on a pagination task — only to end up asking 'is pagination even needed here?'. Articulated an architectural blocker, task closed at the product level. Learned that recognizing a dead end on time is also a result

Picked up a JS bug after a previous attempt — diagnosed it in one pass. In parallel, cleaned up stale branches 500–700 commits behind master: nearly lost code once during conflict resolution — caught it and recovered

months.label: August 2025
entries: Solo feature in a week: SLA timer with external API integration — cache on first page load and webhook to invalidate on data change. Designed the architecture myself, reviewer approved. Six post-deploy days with various error types — but got it to prod

Finished the first version of an analytics dashboard: Django model for data accumulation, periodic task for calculation, frontend with a Graph/Table toggle. Stage showed zeros (periodic tasks don't run there) — decided to push to prod, data came in immediately

Bulk SPF parser for a domain list: instead of sequential processing — a parallel DNS strategy (5 threads × 20 domains). 40 minutes instead of 8 hours; single-threaded the task was practically unsolvable

Email authentication stabilization, 5 tickets: false positive SPF on a non-standard subdomain, DKIM error breakdown on a Cyrillic domain character by character, trailing-character fix via regex with tests

Pagination audit across the entire frontend: automation gave unreliable results, switched to manual walkthrough. Map of three categories — custom pagination, pages without it, and broken standard pagination. Became the foundation for a series of follow-up refactors

Lesson of the month: an urgent evening hotfix under a deadline threw a 500 on an unanticipated data type. Next morning — a type-aware solution and an honest comment 'didn't think it through under pressure'. Takeaway: a boundary-type checklist before hotfix deploys

months.label: July 2025
entries: First production release of a complex module: deployed SPF validation per RFC 7208 — and immediately caught a wave of 7 false positives on real domains. Closed everything in 2 days, surgically: removed redundant checks, fixed unicode IP encoding, added support for non-standard DNS labels. No regressions

Biggest solo feature to that point — an analytics dashboard of audience dynamics by day. Full multi-layer: custom Django model for data accumulation, periodic task, frontend with a Graph/Table toggle and filters. 13 days of development straight, review with changes same day

Support system integration: two cases to prod. First — diagnosing a 'silent' bug where an update seemed to go through but didn't apply; turned out to be a typo in a key. Second — clickable links: the standard Django approach didn't work, independently redefined the solution and moved the logic to JS
Along the way, found and fixed a broken neighboring button ('was near the code — couldn't walk past') and independently caught a timedelta bug: subtracting a number from a date instead of a duration

months.label: June 2025
entries: External block WYSIWYG editor integration: library setup and configuration, iframe proxying, CORS bypass, two-way exchange via postMessage. Full cycle solo — from task analysis to prod: implementation, DB migration, two rounds of review, QA fixes

System module for mail policy syntax validation per RFC 7208: a parser covering 15+ violation types. Not a textbook exercise — the module closed an entire cluster of real support requests where policies were being processed incorrectly
Hunting edge cases in production: unicode in domain labels, specific DNS labels, validator false positives. Three targeted post-prod iterations — each a concrete fix without rewriting the module
External system integration investigation: instead of 'just do something', dug into the third-party API constraints and communicated the nature of the problem to the team
Applied fixes throughout the month: restoring background task queue operation, an API error handler for deleting a linked entity (brought to review, but closed by product decision as unnecessary)

months.label: May 2025
entries: May 12 — first day at work. The first week and a half went entirely to onboarding: exploring a large unfamiliar codebase, reading others' code, trying to understand how it all fits together
First commit to prod — on day 5: took a small task, brought it to release, review passed without a single comment. Small, but an important symbolic start

Main energy of the month — writing tests for a historically uncovered component. Turned out to be the best way to get oriented: you can't write a good test without thoroughly understanding the logic. That's how the tests became a map of the system

Found my own regression: calculation was breaking on the first days of the month because of `-1` instead of `timedelta` when working with dates in Python. Classic trap — didn't just fix it, dug into the root cause and explained it in a comment
